response.title: what solar generator should i buy to keep medicine cold in an outage on a fixed income
response.answer:
For keeping medicine cold during a power outage on a fixed income, I'd recommend a small portable power station rather than an expensive whole-house solar generator.

The most important thing is to buy enough battery capacity to protect your medicine without spending hundreds of dollars more than necessary.

My recommendation depends on whether you're powering a regular household refrigerator or a small refrigerator just for medication.

A few things to know before buying:

You don't necessarily need solar panels. A rechargeable battery power station can keep a refrigerator running during an outage. Solar panels are useful for longer outages but add cost.

Look for a LiFePO4 (LFP) battery. These generally last much longer than older lithium-ion designs.

Avoid very small 200–300Wh units for a full-size refrigerator. They may not have enough capacity or power to run it reliably.

Medicine temperature matters. Many refrigerated medicines must stay between 36°F and 46°F (2°C–8°C), but requirements vary. A refrigerator thermometer is an inexpensive and important addition.

Two power stations worth considering

EcoFlow RIVER 2 Pro Portable Power Station

768Wh battery · 800W output

$499.00

A reasonable option for a small refrigerator or efficient medication cooler. Runtime depends on actual electricity use.

Jackery Explorer 1000 V2 Portable Power Station

1,070Wh battery · 1,500W output

$549.00

My stronger choice for a household refrigerator, provided its starting power requirement is compatible.

These are battery-only prices, without solar panels. Neither guarantees 24 hours of refrigeration without knowing your appliance's power consumption.

For a lower-cost emergency plan, an insulated cooler, reusable cold packs, and a thermometer may be more practical. Keep medicine separated from ice to prevent freezing, and follow its specific storage instructions. 
FDA
+1
